headline: GOLD HITS LOWEST SINCE OCTOBER 2025 — $3,832 on Warsh/Fed Hike Bets; Mining Stocks Fall as $3,800 Bear Target Comes Into View
snippet: Gold dropped to $3,832 in early Asian trading on Monday — its lowest level since October 2025 — before stabilising near $3,872 as markets reacted to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks flagging inflation as a bigger concern than the slowing labour market. The sell-off shook gold mining equities: Agnico Eagle fell 2.34%, Barrick Mining 2.10%, with the broader sector under pressure as rate-hike expectations reassert themselves. The bull scenario requires a close above $4,010 to regain momentum; below $3,800 the technical picture deteriorates sharply.

headline: COPPER FALLS TO FOUR-MONTH LOW ON CHINA WEAK DATA — $6/LB Floor at Risk as Demand Lags Tight Physical Stocks; $5.95 Next Target
snippet: LME copper fell to a four-month low near $6.00–6.06 per pound on November 17, with weak Chinese demand data the primary driver — China's refined copper spot trading remained sluggish even as prices fell, with semis consumption described as mediocre. Despite LME warehouse stocks staying near recent lows (tight physical market), domestic consumption in China has lagged expectations. Technically, $6.00 is now the critical floor; a break puts $5.95 in play. US copper-miner ETFs fell roughly 5.4% overnight, extending the AI-tech sector selloff that began last week.

headline: FREEPORT MOVES INTO TOODOGGONE — C$110M for 51% of TDG Gold's Aurora West in BC's Premier Copper-Gold District
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan has agreed to acquire a 51% interest in TDG Gold Corp's Aurora West project in British Columbia's Toodoggone district for C$110 million in cash at closing, announced November 12. Freeport retains the right to earn up to 75% by spending an additional C$30 million over three years (C$15M in the first two years). TDG keeps its Shasta and Baker properties; the deal needs TSX-V approval and is expected to close after a December corporate reorganisation. The deal is a major validation of the Toodoggone district, where Freeport already holds the Joy project alongside Amarc Resources.

headline: ALTIUS LAUNCHES C$122M TAKEOVER OF TNR GOLD — Spinout Packages Shotgun Alaska Project; 60% Premium, Vote in December
snippet: Altius Minerals agreed on November 11 to acquire the remaining shares of TSX-V-listed TNR Gold it doesn't already own in an all-stock deal valued at approximately C$122 million — a roughly 60% premium to TNR's November 10 close. TNR shareholders receive 0.0072 of an Altius share plus 0.25 of a share in a newly formed spinout holding the Shotgun gold project in Alaska; the spinout will be 88% owned by former TNR shareholders. Closing is expected in Q1 2027 pending shareholder, court and regulatory approvals. The deal ends a months-long board fight with activist shareholder Eucalyptus Resources, which now backs the transaction.

headline: CANADA GOLD OUTPUT SURGES 22% IN Q3 — Valentine Mine, Goose Drive Record Quarter; But Global Supply Slips 1% as Recycling Hits 3-Year Low
snippet: World Gold Council data for Q3 2026 shows Canadian gold mine output jumped 22% year-on-year — the strongest growth among major producers — driven by Equinox Gold's Valentine mine in Newfoundland and B2Gold's Goose mine in Nunavut. Indonesia (+21%) and Chile (+19%) also surged. Global mine production hit a Q3 record of 1,071 tonnes, up 3% YoY. Yet total gold supply fell 1% to 1,368.6 tonnes because recycled gold collapsed 8% to 314.5 tonnes — its lowest since Q4 2023 — as holders refused to sell near multi-month lows. Central bank buying surged 42% in the quarter.

headline: ABRASILVER DRILLS 75m AT 2.44 g/t GOLD, 106 g/t SILVER INSIDE PLANNED MINE — Oculto Argentina Hit Confirms Grade Ahead of Q4 FID Decision
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp (TSX-V: ABBRF) reported drill hole DDH-26-064 at the Oculto deposit, Diablillos project, Salta, Argentina: 75 metres grading 2.44 g/t gold and 106 g/t silver starting at 220 metres depth — entirely within the footprint of the planned open-pit mine. The company is running three drill rigs and targets a final construction decision in Q4 2026. The feasibility study completed in June 2026 outlined proven and probable reserves of 77.9 million tonnes containing an estimated 184 million ounces of silver and 1.8 million ounces of gold.

headline: AUSTRAL RESOURCES ACQUIRES HAMMER METALS — Australian Copper Scheme Effective November 16; Implementation November 25
snippet: The Federal Court of Australia approved the Austral Resources–Hammer Metals scheme of arrangement on November 13, with the acquisition becoming legally effective on November 16 and final implementation scheduled for November 25. The deal consolidates Austral's position in Queensland copper, adding Hammer Metals' project pipeline in the Mount Isa belt to Austral's producing assets. The takeover is part of an accelerating wave of Australian copper consolidation as mid-tier producers build scale ahead of the next demand cycle.

headline: BANNERMAN ETANGO $353M NAMIBIA URANIUM MINE ON SCHEDULE — 2028 First Production Confirmed; 3.5Mlb/yr at $39/lb AISC
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) confirmed construction at the Etango uranium project in Namibia is proceeding on schedule, targeting first yellowcake production in 2028. The project — approved via final investment decision following a September financing deal with CNNC Overseas — has a capital cost of $353 million and forecast annual output of approximately 3.5 million pounds of uranium oxide at an all-in sustaining cost of roughly $39 per pound. Bannerman holds a 55% joint venture interest, with CNNC Overseas (China National Nuclear Corp) holding 45% and providing both construction capital and an offtake commitment for most of the output.

headline: CHINA-LINKED ACTIVISTS BLOCK TRUMP-BACKED CALIFORNIA RARE EARTH MINE — Federal Judge Halts Dateline Expansion at Mojave's Colosseum Deposit
snippet: A federal judge has issued an order halting the expansion of the Colosseum mine in California's Mojave National Preserve into rare earth mining, following a legal challenge from activist groups alleged to have ties to Chinese interests. The Trump administration had backed Australian company Dateline's proposal to convert the historically decommissioned gold mine into a domestic rare earth operation as part of US critical minerals strategy. The case illustrates the geopolitical friction running through US rare earth supply chain development as ex-China REE prices rise and China maintains export licensing controls.

headline: ENDEAVOUR SILVER HITS 3,431 g/t SILVER EQUIV OVER 1.42m AT CONTRARIA — Guanaceví Mexico Vein Opens Multiple New Stope Fronts
snippet: Endeavour Silver Corp (NYSE: EXK) reported results from a 20-hole, 5,855-metre drill program at the Contraria vein, Guanaceví mine, Mexico, with the standout intercept returning 3,431 g/t silver equivalent over 1.42 metres true width. Multiple high-grade intercepts across the program confirm the structural continuity of the Contraria vein and open several new stope fronts that could add near-term ounces to the mine's high-grade inventory. Guanaceví is one of Mexico's highest-grade operating silver mines.

headline: FURY GOLD, B2GOLD, GOLD ROYALTY NAMED AS HEADWIND-PROOF PICKS — Zacks Screens Low-AISC Producers as Gold Tests $3,800 Support
snippet: Zacks Research named Fury Gold Mines, Gold Royalty Corp, Newmont, and B2Gold as the four gold mining companies best positioned to weather the current sector downturn, citing balance sheet strength, low all-in sustaining costs, and project-level growth catalysts. With gold testing multi-month lows near $3,800–$3,872, Zacks argues that AISC discipline — not just gold price leverage — separates the survivors from the casualties in the current rate-driven correction. Newmont's 2026 consensus EPS estimate has been revised up 1.4% over the past 30 days, implying year-over-year growth of 33%.

headline: AMERICAN RARE EARTHS WRAPS WYOMING FEASIBILITY DRILLING — Halleck Creek 2026 Program Complete at US's Largest Known REE Deposit
snippet: American Rare Earths (ASX: ARR) has completed its 2026 feasibility study drill program at the Halleck Creek rare earth project in Wyoming's Cowboy State Mine area, wrapping up the final 12 holes following initial assay results released in September. The program is the foundation for the company's feasibility study at what is described as the largest known rare earth deposit in the United States on a total rare earth oxide basis. Full assay results from the completed program are expected to follow, feeding into an updated NI 43-101-equivalent resource estimate supporting future development decisions.
